abstract: Single source of truth is an important concept in modern data center management practices. It is fundamental to reliably automate the configuration, deployment, and management of resources in large data centers. Legacy media systems that incorporate dedicated resource registries, such as Network Media Open Specification (NMOS), are maladapted to integration into single source of truth data center management systems because they introduce their own, additional, dedicated source of truth. Permitting multiple sources of truth to emanate in a new system to accommodate legacy system integration has the effect of increasing system complexity and decreasing system reliability. Open legacy protocols, such as the NMOS, however, make it feasible to consider new implementations that resolve the legacy maladaptation problem and preserve a new system’s single source of truth design principles.

authors.bio: Jim Trainor has three decades of professional software development experience. Trainor began working in the media industry in 1995 as a software developer at Discreet Logic Inc., and later as a founder of startup DiskStream Inc., and as a software developer at Miranda Inc. Beginning in 2001, Trainor began a long relationship with the Advanced Media Workflow Association (AMWA) as a member and a consultant, performing software development, development of training material, and a short tenure as the head of the AMWA Technical Steering Committee. More recently, Trainor also has experience developing web applications deployed in the cloud, in addition to continued media consulting work. Trainor is based in Canada.
